premises.statement: Applying the two-body Kepler relation directly to TLE mean motion produces the semi-major axis intended by the task without additional TLE mean-element corrections.
premises.reason: The entire drag series will depend on this conversion from mean motion to semi-major axis.

premises.statement: Characters 53–63 of every parsed TLE line 2 contain mean motion in revolutions per day.
premises.reason: Both the field selection and its units control every calculated semi-major axis, but no TLE format reference has established them.

premises.statement: Every consecutive pair in lines is a correctly associated TLE line 1 and line 2 for SATCAT 43180.
premises.target: t and its printed sampling summaries
premises.reason: Mispaired records or records for another satellite would associate incorrect orbital values with epochs.

premises.statement: Each extracted epoch uses a two-digit year in the 2000s followed by a one-based fractional day of year.
premises.reason: The date conversion determines which observations belong to the requested period and their eventual hourly matches.

premises.statement: TLE epoch timestamps and OMNI hourly timestamps use the same time reference, so no time-zone or time-scale conversion is needed before alignment.
premises.reason: A time-reference offset would shift the eventual lag comparison even though the rounding itself follows the task.

fewer.target: Printed duplicate-hour, hour-span, hourly multiplicity, and daily sample-count summaries
fewer.reason: Beyond the shared premise that input pairs represent the intended satellite's records, these descriptive summaries introduce no additional unsupported premises; they explicitly measure duplication and sampling rather than assume them.
